title: Commanding Good and Forbidding Evil
summary: The hadith emphasizes the importance of enjoining good and forbidding evil to avoid divine punishment.
translation: A believer should praise and encourage good deeds, offering help, and try to stop bad deeds to the best of their ability. If unable, they should at least despise them in their heart. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: "By Him in Whose Hand is my soul, you must enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, or Allah will send His punishment upon you. Then you will call upon Him, but He will not respond to you." (Narrated by Tirmidhi) Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) emphasized that performing the duty of enjoining good and forbidding evil brings Allah's mercy and acceptance of prayers. Neglect leads to divine punishment that prayers cannot avert. Another hadith supports this, saying that failure to perform this duty will result in evil people being empowered over you, and even the prayers of the righteous will not be accepted until this duty is resumed.
